passages.provision_quote: B. Athletic teams or sports designated for "females", "women" or "girls" may not be open to students of the male sex. C. This section does not restrict the eligibility of any student to participate in any interscholastic or intramural athletic team or sport designated as being for "males", "men" or "boys" or designated as "coed" or "mixed".
passages.note: Enacted text of SB 1165 (2022), which excludes biological males from female-designated teams while leaving male/coed team eligibility unrestricted.
House Third Reading roll call shows Martinez voted Y on final passage of SB 1165.
Bill status overview confirms SB 1165 passed the House 31-24-5-0-0 and was signed by the Governor.

rows.reasoning: Martinez voted Y in the House Third Reading (Passed 31-24-5-0-0) on SB 1165 (2022), a single-subject bill signed into law, whose operative text provides that teams designated for "females", "women" or "girls" may not be open to students of the male sex while leaving eligibility for male-designated or coed teams unrestricted. This matches the rung requiring transgender athletes to compete only on teams matching their biological sex assigned at birth, and the unrestricted male/coed clause excludes a total ban on competing in any organized sport.
